source.text: וּפְלִשְׁתִּ֖ים נִלְחָמִ֣ים בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיָּנֻ֜סוּ אַנְשֵׁ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מִפְּנֵ֣י פְלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וַיִּפְּל֥וּ חֲלָלִ֖ים בְּהַ֥ר הַגִּלְבֹּֽעַ׃

records.literal_gloss: And Philistines [were] fighting against Israel, and fled [the] men of Israel from before Philistines, and fell slain on [the] mount of the Gilboa.

en.L: And the Philistines were fighting against Israel, and the men of Israel fled from before the Philistines and fell slain on Mount Gilboa.
en.B: Now the Philistines were fighting against Israel. The men of Israel fled from the Philistines, and many fell dead on Mount Gilboa.
en.R: The Philistines fought a battle against Israel. The Israelite soldiers ran away from the Philistines, and many of them were killed on Mount Gilboa.

es.L: Y los filisteos peleaban contra Israel, y los hombres de Israel huyeron de delante de los filisteos, y cayeron muertos en el monte Gilboa.
es.B: Los filisteos estaban peleando contra Israel. Los hombres de Israel huyeron de los filisteos, y muchos cayeron muertos en el monte Gilboa.
es.R: Los filisteos pelearon una batalla contra Israel. Los soldados israelitas huyeron de los filisteos, y a muchos de ellos los mataron en el monte Gilboa.

fr.L: Et les Philistins combattaient contre Israël, et les hommes d’Israël s’enfuirent devant les Philistins, et ils tombèrent blessés à mort sur le mont Guilboa.
fr.B: Les Philistins livraient bataille contre Israël. Les hommes d’Israël s’enfuirent devant les Philistins, et beaucoup tombèrent morts sur le mont Guilboa.
fr.R: Les Philistins se sont battus contre Israël. Les soldats israélites se sont enfuis devant les Philistins, et beaucoup d’entre eux ont été tués sur le mont Guilboa.

sw.L: Wafilisti walikuwa wakipigana na Israeli, na watu wa Israeli wakakimbia mbele ya Wafilisti, wakaanguka wameuawa katika mlima Gilboa.
sw.B: Basi Wafilisti walikuwa wakipigana na Israeli. Watu wa Israeli wakawakimbia Wafilisti, na wengi wakaanguka wamekufa katika mlima Gilboa.
sw.R: Wafilisti wakapigana vita na Israeli. Askari wa Israeli wakawakimbia Wafilisti, na wengi wao wakauawa katika mlima Gilboa.

vi.L: Người Phi-li-tin đánh Y-sơ-ra-ên, và người Y-sơ-ra-ên chạy trốn trước mặt người Phi-li-tin, và bị giết ngã xuống trên núi Ghinh-bô-a.
vi.B: Bấy giờ người Phi-li-tin giao chiến với Y-sơ-ra-ên. Quân Y-sơ-ra-ên bỏ chạy trước mặt người Phi-li-tin, và nhiều người bị giết ngã xuống trên núi Ghinh-bô-a.
vi.R: Người Phi-li-tin đánh trận với Y-sơ-ra-ên. Quân lính Y-sơ-ra-ên bỏ chạy trước người Phi-li-tin, và nhiều người trong số họ bị giết trên núi Ghinh-bô-a.

ko.L: 그리고 블레셋 사람들이 이스라엘과 싸우고 있었는데, 이스라엘 사람들이 블레셋 사람들 앞에서 도망쳤고, 길보아 산에서 죽임을 당해 쓰러졌다.
ko.B: 블레셋 사람들이 이스라엘과 싸웠다. 이스라엘 사람들은 블레셋 사람들 앞에서 달아났고, 많은 사람이 길보아 산에서 죽어 쓰러졌다.
ko.R: 블레셋 사람들이 이스라엘과 전쟁을 했다. 이스라엘 군인들은 블레셋 사람들을 피해 도망쳤고, 그들 가운데 많은 사람이 길보아 산에서 죽임을 당했다.

decisions.choice: the Philistines were fighting: the story returns to the battle that chapters 28 and 29 prepared
decisions.reason: The sentence opens with its subject and an ongoing verb form, not the usual story verb. It picks up the account left at 28:4 and 29:1, 11, where the Philistines gathered and marched north to Jezreel while Saul camped on Gilboa; chapter 30 had followed David in the south. The battle is already under way when the scene opens.

decisions.choice: Mount Gilboa: the ridge on the southeast side of the Jezreel valley
decisions.reason: Saul had camped there before the battle (28:4). The hills rise above the valley where the Philistine chariots and troops were gathered at Shunem and Jezreel (28:4; 29:1).

decisions.choice: 1 Chronicles 10:1-12 retells this chapter
decisions.reason: The Chronicler gives the same account in almost the same words, as the opening of his history of David's reign. The differences are noted at verses 6, 9-10 and 12-13. Its closing verses (1 Chronicles 10:13-14) add the reason for Saul's death: his unfaithfulness to the LORD and his consulting a medium (chapter 28).

decisions.choice: many fell dead (Balanced); many of them were killed (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says the men of Israel "fell slain". Not every man died, since some fled and lived (verse 7), so Balanced and Readable add "many" to keep the sense clear.

decisions.choice: "길보아 산" for Mount Gilboa
decisions.reason: The form the terms of this translation set; 1 Chronicles 10 retells this chapter (meaning decision m3), and the Korean should match there.

source.text: וַיַּדְבְּק֣וּ פְלִשְׁתִּ֔ים אֶת־שָׁא֖וּל וְאֶת־בָּנָ֑יו וַיַּכּ֣וּ פְלִשְׁתִּ֗ים אֶת־יְהוֹנָתָ֧ן וְאֶת־אֲבִינָדָ֛ב וְאֶת־מַלְכִּי־שׁ֖וּעַ בְּנֵ֥י שָׁאֽוּל׃

records.literal_gloss: And pursued closely Philistines Saul and his sons, and struck Philistines Jonathan and Abinadab and Malki-Shua, [the] sons of Saul.

en.L: And the Philistines pursued Saul and his sons closely, and the Philistines struck down Jonathan and Abinadab and Malki-Shua, the sons of Saul.
en.B: The Philistines caught up with Saul and his sons, and they killed Jonathan, Abinadab and Malki-Shua, Saul's sons.
en.R: The Philistines chased Saul and his sons and caught up with them. They killed three of Saul's sons: Jonathan, Abinadab and Malki-Shua.

es.L: Y los filisteos persiguieron de cerca a Saúl y a sus hijos, y los filisteos mataron a Jonatán, a Abinadab y a Malquisúa, hijos de Saúl.
es.B: Los filisteos alcanzaron a Saúl y a sus hijos, y mataron a Jonatán, Abinadab y Malquisúa, hijos de Saúl.
es.R: Los filisteos persiguieron a Saúl y a sus hijos hasta alcanzarlos. Mataron a tres de los hijos de Saúl: Jonatán, Abinadab y Malquisúa.

fr.L: Et les Philistins serrèrent de près Saül et ses fils, et les Philistins frappèrent Jonathan, Abinadab et Malki-Shoua, les fils de Saül.
fr.B: Les Philistins talonnèrent Saül et ses fils, et ils tuèrent Jonathan, Abinadab et Malki-Shoua, les fils de Saül.
fr.R: Les Philistins ont poursuivi Saül et ses fils et ils les ont rattrapés. Ils ont tué trois des fils de Saül : Jonathan, Abinadab et Malki-Shoua.

sw.L: Wafilisti wakaambatana na Sauli na wanawe, nao Wafilisti wakawapiga Yonathani na Abinadabu na Malki-shua, wana wa Sauli.
sw.B: Wafilisti wakawafikia Sauli na wanawe, wakawaua Yonathani, Abinadabu na Malki-shua, wana wa Sauli.
sw.R: Wafilisti wakawafukuza Sauli na wanawe, wakawafikia. Wakawaua wana watatu wa Sauli: Yonathani, Abinadabu na Malki-shua.

vi.L: Người Phi-li-tin đuổi sát theo Sau-lơ và các con trai ông, và người Phi-li-tin giết Giô-na-than, A-bi-na-đáp và Manh-ki-sua, các con trai của Sau-lơ.
vi.B: Người Phi-li-tin đuổi kịp Sau-lơ và các con trai ông, và giết Giô-na-than, A-bi-na-đáp và Manh-ki-sua, các con trai của Sau-lơ.
vi.R: Người Phi-li-tin đuổi theo Sau-lơ và các con trai ông, và bắt kịp họ. Họ giết ba con trai của Sau-lơ là Giô-na-than, A-bi-na-đáp và Manh-ki-sua.

ko.L: 그리고 블레셋 사람들이 사울과 그의 아들들을 바짝 뒤쫓았고, 블레셋 사람들이 사울의 아들들인 요나단과 아비나답과 말기수아를 쳐 죽였다.
ko.B: 블레셋 사람들은 사울과 그의 아들들을 바짝 뒤쫓아, 사울의 아들인 요나단과 아비나답과 말기수아를 죽였다.
ko.R: 블레셋 사람들은 사울과 그의 아들들을 쫓아가 따라잡았다. 그리고 사울의 아들 셋, 곧 요나단과 아비나답과 말기수아를 죽였다.

decisions.choice: pursued closely: kept right on their heels until they caught up
decisions.reason: The verb means to cling or stick to something. In this form it is used of an enemy who keeps so close behind that the one fleeing cannot get away (Judges 18:22; 1 Samuel 14:22).

decisions.choice: Jonathan, Abinadab and Malki-Shua: three of Saul's sons
decisions.reason: Jonathan and Malki-Shua are named in 14:49, together with Ishvi; Abinadab appears here for the first time. Another son, Ish-bosheth (also called Eshbaal), was not in the battle and was later made king by Abner (2 Samuel 2:8-10; 1 Chronicles 8:33). Jonathan's death fulfils, in a bitter way, his own words to David that David would be king (23:17).

decisions.choice: three of Saul's sons
decisions.reason: Readable counts the sons, as verse 6 does, so the reader knows these are not all of Saul's sons.

decisions.choice: Malki-Shoua
decisions.reason: A name not in the terms table, in the usual French transcription, kept the same in Chronicles.

decisions.choice: Malquisúa
decisions.reason: The usual Spanish form of Malki-Shua, one of Saul's sons (m2).

decisions.choice: "wakaambatana na" (L)
decisions.reason: The verb means to cling to or stick close (m1); Literal keeps the picture with "kuambatana na", and Balanced and Readable say the Philistines caught up with them.

decisions.choice: "A-bi-na-đáp" and "Manh-ki-sua"
decisions.reason: The same form for Abinadab as Jesse's son (16:8); "Manh-ki-sua" is the usual Protestant form, kept the same through both books.

decisions.choice: "요나단", "아비나답", "말기수아"
decisions.reason: The form the terms of this translation set for Jonathan, and the usual Protestant Korean forms of the others.

source.text: וַתִּכְבַּ֤ד הַמִּלְחָמָה֙ אֶל־שָׁא֔וּל וַיִּמְצָאֻ֥הוּ הַמּוֹרִ֖ים אֲנָשִׁ֣ים בַּקָּ֑שֶׁת וַיָּ֥חֶל מְאֹ֖ד מֵהַמּוֹרִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And was heavy the battle against Saul, and found him the archers, men with the bow, and he writhed exceedingly from the archers.

en.L: And the battle was heavy against Saul, and the archers, men with the bow, found him, and he writhed greatly because of the archers.
en.B: The fighting pressed hard against Saul. The archers found him with their bows, and he was badly wounded by them.
en.R: The battle around Saul became very fierce. Some Philistine soldiers shot arrows at him and hit him, and he was badly hurt.

es.L: Y se hizo pesada la batalla contra Saúl, y lo hallaron los arqueros, hombres de arco, y se retorció mucho a causa de los arqueros.
es.B: La lucha se hizo muy dura en torno a Saúl. Los arqueros lo alcanzaron con sus flechas, y quedó gravemente herido.
es.R: La batalla alrededor de Saúl se volvió muy violenta. Unos soldados filisteos le dispararon flechas y lo alcanzaron, y quedó muy mal herido.

fr.L: Et le combat fut lourd contre Saül, et les archers, les hommes à l’arc, le trouvèrent, et il se tordit de douleur à cause des archers.
fr.B: Le combat se fit acharné autour de Saül. Les archers l’atteignirent de leurs flèches, et il fut gravement blessé par eux.
fr.R: Le combat autour de Saül est devenu très violent. Des soldats philistins lui ont tiré des flèches et l’ont touché, et il a été gravement blessé.

sw.L: Vita vikawa vizito juu ya Sauli, na wapiga upinde, watu wenye upinde, wakampata, naye akagaagaa sana kwa sababu ya wapiga upinde.
sw.B: Mapigano yakamwelemea Sauli. Wapiga upinde wakampata kwa mishale yao, naye akajeruhiwa vibaya nao.
sw.R: Vita vikawa vikali sana kumzunguka Sauli. Baadhi ya askari wa Wafilisti wakamtupia mishale, wakampata, naye akaumia vibaya sana.

vi.L: Trận chiến dồn nặng lên Sau-lơ; các xạ thủ, những người cầm cung, tìm thấy ông, và ông quằn quại đau đớn vì các xạ thủ.
vi.B: Trận đánh dồn dập quanh Sau-lơ. Các xạ thủ tìm thấy ông bằng cung tên, và ông bị họ bắn trọng thương.
vi.R: Trận đánh quanh Sau-lơ trở nên rất ác liệt. Mấy người lính Phi-li-tin bắn tên trúng ông, và ông bị thương nặng.

ko.L: 그리고 사울을 향한 싸움이 격렬해졌다. 활 쏘는 사람들, 곧 활을 가진 사람들이 그를 찾아냈고, 그는 활 쏘는 사람들 때문에 몹시 괴로워했다.
ko.B: 사울을 둘러싼 싸움이 치열해졌다. 활 쏘는 군사들이 그를 찾아내어 활을 쏘았고, 사울은 그들의 화살에 맞아 크게 다쳤다.
ko.R: 사울 주위의 싸움은 아주 치열해졌다. 블레셋 군인 몇이 사울에게 활을 쏘아 맞혔다. 사울은 크게 다쳤다.

decisions.choice: the battle was heavy against Saul: the fighting closed in on him with full force
decisions.reason: "Heavy" describes something that weighs down on a person. The enemy concentrated their attack where the king was.

decisions.choice: he writhed greatly: he was badly wounded and in great pain
alternatives: he trembled with fear because of the archers
decisions.reason: The verb means to writhe or tremble, as in pain or in fear. Since the archers have just found him, and Saul then asks to be killed before the enemy reach him, the sense is most likely that he was wounded. It could also mean that he trembled in terror at the archers. 1 Chronicles 10:3 has the same word.

decisions.choice: found him: the archers reached him and hit him
decisions.reason: "Found" in a battle means caught up with or reached. The added "men with the bow" makes plain who they were: soldiers who could strike from a distance.

decisions.choice: shot arrows at him and hit him
decisions.reason: Readable says what it means for archers to "find" a man in battle, and names them as Philistines.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שָׁאוּל֩ לְנֹשֵׂ֨א כֵלָ֜יו שְׁלֹ֥ף חַרְבְּךָ֣׀וְדָקְרֵ֣נִי בָ֗הּ פֶּן־יָ֠בוֹאוּ הָעֲרֵלִ֨ים הָאֵ֤לֶּה וּדְקָרֻ֨נִי֙ וְהִתְעַלְּלוּ־בִ֔י וְלֹ֤א אָבָה֙ נֹשֵׂ֣א כֵלָ֔יו כִּ֥י יָרֵ֖א מְאֹ֑ד וַיִּקַּ֤ח שָׁאוּל֙ אֶת־הַחֶ֔רֶב וַיִּפֹּ֖ל עָלֶֽיהָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Saul to [the] bearer of his armor, Draw your sword and pierce me with it, lest come these uncircumcised and pierce me and deal wantonly with me; and not was willing the bearer of his armor, for he was afraid exceedingly; and took Saul the sword and fell on it.

en.L: And Saul said to his armor-bearer, "Draw your sword and run me through with it, lest these uncircumcised come and run me through and abuse me." But his armor-bearer was not willing, for he was greatly afraid. And Saul took the sword and fell on it.
en.B: Saul said to his armor-bearer, "Draw your sword and run me through with it, or these uncircumcised men will come and run me through and make sport of me." But his armor-bearer would not do it, because he was terrified. So Saul took his own sword and fell on it.
en.R: Saul said to the young man who carried his armor, "Take out your sword and kill me with it. If you do not, these Philistines, who are outside God's covenant, will come and kill me, and they will treat me cruelly for fun." But the young man would not do it, because he was very much afraid. So Saul took his own sword and fell on it.

es.L: Y dijo Saúl a su escudero: «Saca tu espada y traspásame con ella, no sea que vengan estos incircuncisos y me traspasen y hagan escarnio de mí». Pero su escudero no quiso, porque tenía mucho miedo. Y tomó Saúl la espada y se echó sobre ella.
es.B: Saúl le dijo a su escudero: «Saca tu espada y atraviésame con ella, no sea que vengan estos incircuncisos y me atraviesen y se diviertan conmigo». Pero su escudero no quiso hacerlo, porque estaba aterrado. Entonces Saúl tomó su propia espada y se echó sobre ella.
es.R: Saúl le dijo al joven que le llevaba la armadura: «Saca tu espada y mátame con ella. Si no lo haces, estos filisteos, que están fuera del pacto de Dios, vendrán y me matarán, y se divertirán torturándome». Pero el joven no quiso hacerlo, porque tenía mucho miedo. Así que Saúl tomó su propia espada y se echó sobre ella.

fr.L: Et Saül dit à son porteur d’armes : « Tire ton épée et transperce-moi avec elle, de peur que ces incirconcis ne viennent me transpercer et me maltraiter. » Mais son porteur d’armes ne voulut pas, car il avait très peur. Et Saül prit l’épée et se jeta dessus.
fr.B: Saül dit à son écuyer : « Tire ton épée et transperce-moi, sinon ces incirconcis vont venir me transpercer et s’amuser de moi. » Mais son écuyer refusa, car il était terrifié. Alors Saül prit sa propre épée et se jeta dessus.
fr.R: Saül a dit au jeune homme qui portait ses armes : « Sors ton épée et tue-moi avec. Sinon, ces Philistins, qui ne font pas partie de l’alliance de Dieu, vont venir me tuer, et ils vont me maltraiter pour s’amuser. » Mais le jeune homme n’a pas voulu, parce qu’il avait très peur. Alors Saül a pris sa propre épée et il s’est jeté dessus.

sw.L: Sauli akamwambia mbeba silaha wake, "Chomoa upanga wako, unichome nao, wasije hawa wasiotahiriwa wakanichoma na kunidhalilisha." Lakini mbeba silaha wake hakutaka, kwa maana aliogopa sana. Sauli akachukua upanga, akauangukia.
sw.B: Sauli akamwambia mbeba silaha wake, "Chomoa upanga wako unichome nao, la sivyo watu hawa wasiotahiriwa watakuja kunichoma na kunifanyia mzaha." Lakini mbeba silaha wake hakukubali, kwa sababu aliogopa mno. Basi Sauli akachukua upanga wake mwenyewe, akauangukia.
sw.R: Sauli akamwambia kijana aliyembebea silaha, "Chomoa upanga wako uniue nao. Usipofanya hivyo, Wafilisti hawa walio nje ya agano la Mungu watakuja kuniua, na watanitesa kwa kujifurahisha." Lakini kijana huyo hakukubali, kwa sababu aliogopa sana. Basi Sauli akachukua upanga wake mwenyewe, akauangukia.

vi.L: Sau-lơ nói với người mang khí giới cho mình: "Hãy rút gươm ngươi ra và đâm ta, kẻo những kẻ không chịu cắt bì này đến đâm ta và hành hạ ta." Nhưng người mang khí giới không chịu, vì rất sợ hãi. Sau-lơ lấy gươm và ngã lên trên.
vi.B: Sau-lơ bảo người mang khí giới cho mình: "Hãy rút gươm ra đâm ta đi, kẻo những kẻ không chịu cắt bì này đến đâm ta và làm nhục ta." Nhưng người mang khí giới không dám làm, vì quá kinh hãi. Vậy Sau-lơ lấy chính gươm mình và ngã lên trên.
vi.R: Sau-lơ nói với chàng trai mang áo giáp cho mình: "Hãy rút gươm ra và giết ta đi. Nếu không, những người Phi-li-tin không thuộc về giao ước của Đức Chúa Trời này sẽ đến giết ta, và chúng sẽ hành hạ ta cho vui." Nhưng chàng trai không dám làm, vì quá sợ hãi. Vậy Sau-lơ lấy chính gươm mình và ngã lên trên.

ko.L: 그리고 사울이 자기 무기를 드는 자에게 말했다. "네 칼을 빼서 그것으로 나를 찔러라. 이 할례를 받지 않은 자들이 와서 나를 찌르고 나를 가지고 놀까 두렵다." 그러나 그의 무기를 드는 자는 몹시 두려워서 그렇게 하려고 하지 않았다. 그래서 사울이 칼을 가져다가 그 위에 엎어졌다.
ko.B: 사울이 자기 무기를 드는 사람에게 말했다. "네 칼을 빼서 나를 찔러라. 그렇지 않으면 할례를 받지 않은 이자들이 와서 나를 찌르고 나를 조롱거리로 삼을 것이다." 그러나 그의 무기를 드는 사람은 너무 두려워서 그렇게 하지 못했다. 그래서 사울은 자기 칼을 뽑아 그 위에 엎어졌다.
ko.R: 사울이 자기 갑옷과 무기를 들고 다니는 젊은이에게 말했다. "칼을 빼서 나를 죽여라. 그렇지 않으면 하나님과 언약을 맺지 않은 이 블레셋 사람들이 와서 나를 죽이고, 재미 삼아 나를 괴롭힐 것이다." 그러나 그 젊은이는 너무 무서워서 그렇게 하지 못했다. 그래서 사울은 자기 칼을 가져다가 그 위에 엎어졌다.

decisions.choice: uncircumcised: outsiders to Yahweh's covenant, said with scorn
decisions.reason: As in 14:6 and 17:26, 36, the word sets the Philistines apart as people who do not bear the sign of the covenant with Abraham (Genesis 17:10-14).

decisions.choice: abuse me: make sport of me, treat me cruelly for their own pleasure
decisions.reason: The verb is used of someone who has power over another and uses it to mock or mistreat them: Yahweh dealing with Egypt (Exodus 10:2), the men of Gibeah with the concubine (Judges 19:25). Saul fears torture and public humiliation, as happened to Samson (Judges 16:21-25).

decisions.choice: he was not willing, for he was greatly afraid
decisions.reason: The text gives no more reason than his fear. To kill the king, even at his command, was a fearful thing; David later refuses to lay a hand on the LORD's anointed (24:7; 26:9) and has the man who claims to have killed Saul put to death (2 Samuel 1:14-16).

decisions.choice: Saul fell on his own sword
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 1:6-10 gives a different account, told by an Amalekite who says he killed Saul at Saul's own request and brings David the crown. This chapter, the narrator's account, says Saul died by his own hand, so the Amalekite's story is best read as a lie told to win David's favor.

decisions.choice: run me through
decisions.reason: The verb means to pierce or stab through. "Run me through" keeps the picture of a thrust with a sword at both places in the verse.

decisions.choice: these Philistines, who are outside God's covenant
decisions.reason: Readable names the enemy and explains "uncircumcised" by what it meant, as 14:6 does, and says "the young man who carried his armor" for the title "armor-bearer".

decisions.choice: hagan escarnio de mí (L); se diviertan conmigo (B)
decisions.reason: To make sport of a man, treating him cruelly for pleasure (m2); Readable says it plainly, as the English does. “Escudero” for the armor-bearer at Literal and Balanced, as in 16:21.

decisions.choice: Saul says "ta" and "ngươi" to his armour-bearer
decisions.reason: As the king to his servant throughout the block.

decisions.choice: Saul speaks to his armor-bearer in the plain style (해라체); "할례를 받지 않은" (L, B), "하나님과 언약을 맺지 않은" (R)
decisions.reason: As the king to his attendant; "uncircumcised" in the form the terms of this translation set, explained at Readable as in 17:26.

source.text: וַיַּ֥רְא נֹשֵֽׂא־כֵלָ֖יו כִּ֣י מֵ֣ת שָׁא֑וּל וַיִּפֹּ֥ל גַּם־ה֛וּא עַל־חַרְבּ֖וֹ וַיָּ֥מָת עִמּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And saw [the] bearer of his armor that had died Saul, and fell also he on his sword and died with him.

en.L: And his armor-bearer saw that Saul had died, and he also fell on his sword and died with him.
en.B: Seeing that Saul was dead, his armor-bearer also fell on his own sword, and he died with him.
en.R: When the young man saw that Saul was dead, he also fell on his own sword. He died there with Saul.

es.L: Y vio su escudero que Saúl había muerto, y también él se echó sobre su espada y murió con él.
es.B: Al ver que Saúl estaba muerto, su escudero también se echó sobre su propia espada y murió con él.
es.R: Cuando el joven vio que Saúl estaba muerto, también se echó sobre su propia espada. Murió allí con Saúl.

fr.L: Et son porteur d’armes vit que Saül était mort, et lui aussi se jeta sur son épée et mourut avec lui.
fr.B: Voyant que Saül était mort, son écuyer se jeta lui aussi sur sa propre épée et mourut avec lui.
fr.R: Quand le jeune homme a vu que Saül était mort, il s’est jeté lui aussi sur sa propre épée. Il est mort là, avec Saül.

sw.L: Mbeba silaha wake akaona kwamba Sauli amekufa, naye pia akauangukia upanga wake, akafa pamoja naye.
sw.B: Mbeba silaha wake alipoona kwamba Sauli amekufa, naye pia akauangukia upanga wake mwenyewe, akafa pamoja naye.
sw.R: Kijana yule alipoona kwamba Sauli amekufa, naye pia akauangukia upanga wake mwenyewe. Akafa pale pamoja na Sauli.

vi.L: Người mang khí giới thấy Sau-lơ đã chết, thì cũng ngã lên gươm mình và chết với ông.
vi.B: Thấy Sau-lơ đã chết, người mang khí giới cũng ngã lên gươm mình và chết với ông.
vi.R: Khi chàng trai thấy Sau-lơ đã chết, anh cũng ngã lên gươm mình. Anh chết ở đó cùng với Sau-lơ.

ko.L: 그리고 그의 무기를 드는 자가 사울이 죽은 것을 보고, 그도 자기 칼 위에 엎어져 그와 함께 죽었다.
ko.B: 그의 무기를 드는 사람은 사울이 죽은 것을 보고 자기도 칼 위에 엎어져 사울과 함께 죽었다.
ko.R: 그 젊은이는 사울이 죽은 것을 보고, 자기도 자기 칼 위에 엎어졌다. 그는 그곳에서 사울과 함께 죽었다.

decisions.choice: he also: the armor-bearer does what his master did
decisions.reason: The emphatic "he also" ties his death to Saul's. The man who would not kill the king will not outlive him either.

decisions.choice: the young man
decisions.reason: Readable keeps calling him "the young man" as in verse 4, so the reader can follow who is meant.

source.text: וַיָּ֣מָת שָׁא֡וּל וּשְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת בָּנָיו֩ וְנֹשֵׂ֨א כֵלָ֜יו גַּ֧ם כָּל־אֲנָשָׁ֛יו בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא יַחְדָּֽו׃

records.literal_gloss: And died Saul and three [of] his sons and [the] bearer of his armor, also all his men, on the day the that together.

en.L: And Saul died, and his three sons, and his armor-bearer, and also all his men, on that day together.
en.B: So Saul died, with his three sons and his armor-bearer and all his men, together on that same day.
en.R: So Saul, his three sons, the young man who carried his armor, and all of Saul's men died together on that one day.

es.L: Y murieron Saúl y sus tres hijos y su escudero, y también todos sus hombres, aquel día juntamente.
es.B: Así murieron juntos aquel mismo día Saúl, sus tres hijos, su escudero y todos sus hombres.
es.R: Así que Saúl, sus tres hijos, el joven que le llevaba la armadura y todos los hombres de Saúl murieron juntos en un mismo día.

fr.L: Et Saül mourut, et ses trois fils, et son porteur d’armes, et aussi tous ses hommes, ce jour-là, ensemble.
fr.B: Ainsi moururent ensemble, ce même jour, Saül, ses trois fils, son écuyer et tous ses hommes.
fr.R: Ainsi, Saül, ses trois fils, le jeune homme qui portait ses armes et tous les hommes de Saül sont morts ensemble ce jour-là.

sw.L: Sauli akafa, na wanawe watatu, na mbeba silaha wake, na watu wake wote pia, siku ile pamoja.
sw.B: Hivyo Sauli akafa, pamoja na wanawe watatu, mbeba silaha wake na watu wake wote, siku ile ile pamoja.
sw.R: Hivyo Sauli, wanawe watatu, kijana aliyembebea silaha, na watu wote wa Sauli wakafa pamoja siku ile moja.

vi.L: Vậy Sau-lơ chết, cùng với ba con trai ông, người mang khí giới cho ông, và cả tất cả những người của ông, trong cùng một ngày đó.
vi.B: Như vậy Sau-lơ đã chết, cùng với ba con trai ông, người mang khí giới cho ông và tất cả những người của ông, trong cùng một ngày.
vi.R: Như vậy, Sau-lơ, ba con trai ông, chàng trai mang áo giáp cho ông, và tất cả những người của Sau-lơ đều chết chung trong một ngày.

ko.L: 그리고 사울과 그의 세 아들과 그의 무기를 드는 자와 그의 모든 부하가 그날 함께 죽었다.
ko.B: 이렇게 사울과 그의 세 아들과 그의 무기를 드는 사람과 그의 모든 부하가 그날 함께 죽었다.
ko.R: 이렇게 사울과 그의 세 아들과 그의 갑옷과 무기를 들고 다니던 젊은이와 사울의 모든 부하가 그날 하루에 다 함께 죽었다.

decisions.choice: Samuel's word fulfilled: Saul and his sons die on the day of the battle
decisions.reason: The night before, Samuel had told Saul at En-dor that the LORD would give Israel into the hand of the Philistines, and "tomorrow you and your sons will be with me" (28:19). The very next day it happens.

decisions.choice: all his men: the men around Saul, his own troops and guard
decisions.reason: Not every soldier of Israel died, since some fled and survived (verse 7). The phrase means the men who stood with Saul himself. 1 Chronicles 10:6 says instead "and all his house died together", seeing the end of Saul's royal line in that day, though one son, Ish-bosheth, and a grandson, Mephibosheth, lived on (2 Samuel 2:8; 4:4).

decisions.choice: together: all on the same day, in the same defeat
decisions.reason: "Together" stresses that the king, his heirs and his men fell at one stroke; Saul's house loses both its king and his successors at once.

source.text: וַיִּרְא֣וּ אַנְשֵֽׁי־יִ֠שְׂרָאֵל אֲשֶׁר־בְּעֵ֨בֶר הָעֵ֜מֶק וַאֲשֶׁ֣ר׀בְּעֵ֣בֶר הַיַּרְדֵּ֗ן כִּֽי־נָ֨סוּ֙ אַנְשֵׁ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְכִי־מֵ֖תוּ שָׁא֣וּל וּבָנָ֑יו וַיַּעַזְב֤וּ אֶת־הֶֽעָרִים֙ וַיָּנֻ֔סוּ וַיָּבֹ֣אוּ פְלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וַיֵּֽשְׁב֖וּ בָּהֶֽן׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And saw [the] men of Israel who [were] on [the] other side of the valley and who [were] on [the] other side of the Jordan that had fled [the] men of Israel, and that had died Saul and his sons, and they abandoned the cities and fled; and came Philistines and lived in them.

en.L: And the men of Israel who [were] on the other side of the valley and who [were] beyond the Jordan saw that the men of Israel had fled and that Saul and his sons had died, and they abandoned the cities and fled; and the Philistines came and lived in them.
en.B: When the men of Israel on the other side of the valley and beyond the Jordan saw that Israel's army had fled and that Saul and his sons were dead, they abandoned their towns and fled. Then the Philistines came and settled in them.
en.R: Other Israelites lived across the valley and on the other side of the Jordan River. They saw that Israel's army had run away and that Saul and his sons were dead. So they left their towns and ran away, and the Philistines came and lived in those towns.

es.L: Y vieron los hombres de Israel que [estaban] al otro lado del valle y que [estaban] al otro lado del Jordán que los hombres de Israel habían huido, y que Saúl y sus hijos habían muerto, y abandonaron las ciudades y huyeron; y vinieron los filisteos y habitaron en ellas.
es.B: Cuando los hombres de Israel que vivían al otro lado del valle y al otro lado del Jordán vieron que el ejército de Israel había huido y que Saúl y sus hijos habían muerto, abandonaron sus ciudades y huyeron. Entonces vinieron los filisteos y se establecieron en ellas.
es.R: Otros israelitas vivían al otro lado del valle y al otro lado del río Jordán. Vieron que el ejército de Israel había huido y que Saúl y sus hijos habían muerto. Así que abandonaron sus pueblos y huyeron, y los filisteos vinieron a vivir en esos pueblos.

fr.L: Et les hommes d’Israël qui [étaient] de l’autre côté de la vallée et qui [étaient] au-delà du Jourdain virent que les hommes d’Israël s’étaient enfuis et que Saül et ses fils étaient morts, et ils abandonnèrent les villes et s’enfuirent ; et les Philistins vinrent et y habitèrent.
fr.B: Quand les hommes d’Israël qui étaient de l’autre côté de la vallée et au-delà du Jourdain virent que l’armée d’Israël s’était enfuie et que Saül et ses fils étaient morts, ils abandonnèrent leurs villes et s’enfuirent. Alors les Philistins vinrent s’y installer.
fr.R: D’autres Israélites habitaient de l’autre côté de la vallée et de l’autre côté du Jourdain. Ils ont vu que l’armée d’Israël s’était enfuie et que Saül et ses fils étaient morts. Alors ils ont quitté leurs villes et ils se sont enfuis, et les Philistins sont venus habiter dans ces villes.

sw.L: Watu wa Israeli waliokuwa ng'ambo ya bonde na waliokuwa ng'ambo ya Yordani wakaona kwamba watu wa Israeli wamekimbia, na kwamba Sauli na wanawe wamekufa, wakaiacha miji, wakakimbia; nao Wafilisti wakaja, wakakaa ndani yake.
sw.B: Watu wa Israeli waliokuwa upande wa pili wa bonde na ng'ambo ya Yordani walipoona kwamba jeshi la Israeli limekimbia na kwamba Sauli na wanawe wamekufa, wakaiacha miji yao, wakakimbia. Kisha Wafilisti wakaja, wakakaa ndani yake.
sw.R: Waisraeli wengine waliishi upande wa pili wa bonde na ng'ambo ya mto Yordani. Waliona kwamba jeshi la Israeli limekimbia na kwamba Sauli na wanawe wamekufa. Kwa hiyo wakaiacha miji yao, wakakimbia, nao Wafilisti wakaja, wakaishi katika miji hiyo.

vi.L: Những người Y-sơ-ra-ên ở bên kia thung lũng và ở bên kia sông Giô-đanh thấy rằng người Y-sơ-ra-ên đã chạy trốn, và Sau-lơ cùng các con trai ông đã chết, thì bỏ các thành mà chạy trốn; người Phi-li-tin đến ở trong các thành ấy.
vi.B: Khi những người Y-sơ-ra-ên ở bên kia thung lũng và bên kia sông Giô-đanh thấy quân Y-sơ-ra-ên đã bỏ chạy, và Sau-lơ cùng các con trai ông đã chết, họ bỏ các thành của mình mà chạy trốn. Bấy giờ người Phi-li-tin đến định cư trong các thành ấy.
vi.R: Có những người Y-sơ-ra-ên khác sống bên kia thung lũng và bên kia sông Giô-đanh. Họ thấy quân Y-sơ-ra-ên đã bỏ chạy, và Sau-lơ cùng các con trai ông đã chết. Vì vậy họ bỏ các thành của mình mà chạy trốn, và người Phi-li-tin đến ở trong các thành ấy.

ko.L: 그리고 골짜기 건너편과 요단 건너편에 있던 이스라엘 사람들이, 이스라엘 사람들이 도망쳤고 사울과 그의 아들들이 죽은 것을 보고, 성읍들을 버리고 도망쳤다. 그러자 블레셋 사람들이 와서 그곳에 살았다.
ko.B: 골짜기 건너편과 요단강 건너편에 사는 이스라엘 사람들은 이스라엘 군대가 도망치고 사울과 그의 아들들이 죽은 것을 보고, 자기들의 성읍을 버리고 달아났다. 그러자 블레셋 사람들이 와서 그곳에 자리를 잡고 살았다.
ko.R: 골짜기 건너편과 요단강 건너편에도 이스라엘 사람들이 살고 있었다. 그들은 이스라엘 군대가 도망치고 사울과 그의 아들들이 죽은 것을 보았다. 그래서 그들은 자기 마을을 버리고 도망쳤다. 그러자 블레셋 사람들이 와서 그 마을들에 살았다.

decisions.choice: the other side of the valley: the far side of the Jezreel valley from Gilboa
decisions.reason: The battle was fought at the edge of the broad valley of Jezreel (29:1). The Israelites living to the north and east of it were cut off once the army broke.

decisions.choice: beyond the Jordan: the land near and across the Jordan, east of the battlefield
alternatives: the towns on this side of the Jordan, in the Jordan valley
decisions.reason: The phrase usually means the land east of the river, as in Joshua 1:14. Here it may mean the towns along the Jordan valley on either bank, near Beth-shan (verse 10). Either way, the defeat opened the whole region to the Philistines. 1 Chronicles 10:7 has only "all the men of Israel who were in the valley".

decisions.choice: the men of Israel had fled: the army in the battle
decisions.reason: The same phrase names two groups: those living in the region who see, and the army that fled from Gilboa (verse 1). The army's flight is what they see.

decisions.choice: Israel's army
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "army" for the second "men of Israel" so the two groups are not confused.

decisions.choice: towns
decisions.reason: The word covers any walled settlement, large or small; these were country towns, so Balanced and Readable say "towns".

source.text: וַֽיְהִי֙ מִֽמָּחֳרָ֔ת וַיָּבֹ֣אוּ פְלִשְׁתִּ֔ים לְפַשֵּׁ֖ט אֶת־הַחֲלָלִ֑ים וַֽיִּמְצְא֤וּ אֶת־שָׁאוּל֙ וְאֶת־שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת בָּנָ֔יו נֹפְלִ֖ים בְּהַ֥ר הַגִּלְבֹּֽעַ׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was on [the] next day, and came Philistines to strip the slain, and they found Saul and three [of] his sons fallen on [the] mount of the Gilboa.

en.L: And it happened on the next day, when the Philistines came to strip the slain, that they found Saul and his three sons fallen on Mount Gilboa.
en.B: On the next day the Philistines came to strip the dead, and they found Saul and his three sons lying where they had fallen on Mount Gilboa.
en.R: The next day the Philistines came to take the weapons and clothing from the dead bodies. They found the bodies of Saul and his three sons on Mount Gilboa.

es.L: Y sucedió al día siguiente que, cuando los filisteos vinieron a despojar a los muertos, hallaron a Saúl y a sus tres hijos caídos en el monte Gilboa.
es.B: Al día siguiente, los filisteos vinieron a despojar a los muertos y encontraron a Saúl y a sus tres hijos tendidos donde habían caído, en el monte Gilboa.
es.R: Al día siguiente, los filisteos vinieron a quitarles las armas y la ropa a los muertos. Encontraron los cuerpos de Saúl y de sus tres hijos en el monte Gilboa.

fr.L: Et il arriva, le lendemain, quand les Philistins vinrent dépouiller les morts, qu’ils trouvèrent Saül et ses trois fils tombés sur le mont Guilboa.
fr.B: Le lendemain, les Philistins vinrent dépouiller les morts, et ils trouvèrent Saül et ses trois fils étendus là où ils étaient tombés, sur le mont Guilboa.
fr.R: Le lendemain, les Philistins sont venus prendre les armes et les vêtements des morts. Ils ont trouvé les corps de Saül et de ses trois fils sur le mont Guilboa.

sw.L: Ikawa siku iliyofuata, Wafilisti walipokuja kuwavua waliouawa, wakamkuta Sauli na wanawe watatu wameanguka katika mlima Gilboa.
sw.B: Siku iliyofuata Wafilisti wakaja kuwavua wafu, wakamkuta Sauli na wanawe watatu wamelala pale walipoanguka katika mlima Gilboa.
sw.R: Siku iliyofuata Wafilisti wakaja kuchukua silaha na nguo za maiti. Wakazikuta maiti za Sauli na wanawe watatu katika mlima Gilboa.

vi.L: Ngày hôm sau, khi người Phi-li-tin đến lột đồ những người bị giết, họ thấy Sau-lơ và ba con trai ông ngã chết trên núi Ghinh-bô-a.
vi.B: Ngày hôm sau, người Phi-li-tin đến lột đồ những người chết, và họ thấy Sau-lơ cùng ba con trai ông nằm chết trên núi Ghinh-bô-a.
vi.R: Ngày hôm sau, người Phi-li-tin đến lấy vũ khí và quần áo của những xác chết. Họ thấy xác của Sau-lơ và ba con trai ông trên núi Ghinh-bô-a.

ko.L: 그리고 이튿날 블레셋 사람들이 죽은 자들의 [옷을] 벗기러 왔다가, 사울과 그의 세 아들이 길보아 산에 쓰러져 있는 것을 찾았다.
ko.B: 이튿날 블레셋 사람들이 죽은 사람들의 옷과 무기를 벗기러 왔다가, 사울과 그의 세 아들이 길보아 산에 쓰러져 있는 것을 발견했다.
ko.R: 다음 날 블레셋 사람들이 죽은 사람들의 무기와 옷을 가져가려고 왔다. 그들은 길보아 산에서 사울과 그의 세 아들의 시체를 찾아냈다.

decisions.choice: to strip the slain: to take weapons, armor and clothing from the dead
decisions.reason: After a battle the winners went over the field and took whatever was of value from the dead. It was part of the plunder of war, as David took Goliath's weapons (17:54).

decisions.choice: fallen on Mount Gilboa: lying where they had died
decisions.reason: The phrase repeats the words of verse 1, "fell ... on Mount Gilboa". The king and his sons lie among the rest of the slain.

decisions.choice: to take the weapons and clothing from the dead bodies
decisions.reason: Readable explains what stripping the slain meant.

source.text: וַֽיִּכְרְתוּ֙ אֶת־רֹאשׁ֔וֹ וַיַּפְשִׁ֖יטוּ אֶת־כֵּלָ֑יו וַיְשַׁלְּח֨וּ בְאֶֽרֶץ־פְּלִשְׁתִּ֜ים סָבִ֗יב לְבַשֵּׂ֛ר בֵּ֥ית עֲצַבֵּיהֶ֖ם וְאֶת־הָעָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And they cut off his head and stripped off his armor, and sent in [the] land of Philistines all around to bear news [to the] house of their idols and the people.

en.L: And they cut off his head and stripped off his armor, and sent [messengers] into the land of the Philistines all around, to bring the news [to the] house of their idols and the people.
en.B: They cut off Saul's head and stripped off his armor, and they sent messengers throughout the land of the Philistines to carry the good news to the temples of their idols and to the people.
en.R: They cut off Saul's head and took his armor. Then they sent messengers all over the Philistine land to tell the good news in the temples of their idols and to all their people.

es.L: Y le cortaron la cabeza y le quitaron la armadura, y enviaron [mensajeros] por la tierra de los filisteos alrededor, para llevar la noticia [a la] casa de sus ídolos y al pueblo.
es.B: Le cortaron la cabeza a Saúl y le quitaron la armadura, y enviaron mensajeros por toda la tierra de los filisteos para anunciar la buena noticia en los templos de sus ídolos y al pueblo.
es.R: Le cortaron la cabeza a Saúl y le quitaron la armadura. Luego enviaron mensajeros por toda la tierra filistea para dar la buena noticia en los templos de sus ídolos y a toda su gente.

fr.L: Et ils lui coupèrent la tête et lui ôtèrent ses armes, et ils envoyèrent [des messagers] dans le pays des Philistins, tout autour, pour porter la nouvelle [dans] la maison de leurs idoles et au peuple.
fr.B: Ils coupèrent la tête de Saül et lui retirèrent ses armes, et ils envoyèrent des messagers dans tout le pays des Philistins pour annoncer la bonne nouvelle dans les temples de leurs idoles et au peuple.
fr.R: Ils ont coupé la tête de Saül et ils ont pris ses armes. Ensuite, ils ont envoyé des messagers dans tout le pays des Philistins pour annoncer la bonne nouvelle dans les temples de leurs idoles et à tout leur peuple.

sw.L: Wakakikata kichwa chake, wakamvua silaha zake, wakatuma [wajumbe] katika nchi ya Wafilisti pande zote, kupeleka habari njema [katika] nyumba ya sanamu zao na kwa watu.
sw.B: Wakakikata kichwa cha Sauli, wakamvua silaha zake, wakatuma wajumbe katika nchi yote ya Wafilisti kupeleka habari njema katika mahekalu ya sanamu zao na kwa watu.
sw.R: Wakakikata kichwa cha Sauli, wakachukua silaha zake. Kisha wakatuma wajumbe kila mahali katika nchi ya Wafilisti kutangaza habari njema katika mahekalu ya sanamu zao na kwa watu wao wote.

vi.L: Họ cắt đầu ông và lột áo giáp ông, rồi sai [người] đi khắp xứ Phi-li-tin để báo tin mừng [cho] đền miếu các thần tượng của họ và cho dân chúng.
vi.B: Họ cắt đầu Sau-lơ và lột áo giáp ông, rồi sai sứ giả đi khắp xứ Phi-li-tin để báo tin mừng trong các đền miếu thần tượng của họ và cho dân chúng.
vi.R: Họ cắt đầu Sau-lơ và lấy áo giáp của ông. Rồi họ sai sứ giả đi khắp xứ Phi-li-tin để loan báo tin mừng trong các đền thờ thần tượng của họ và cho toàn dân.

ko.L: 그리고 그들이 그의 머리를 베고 그의 갑옷을 벗기고, 블레셋 사람들의 땅 사방으로 [사람을] 보내어 그들의 우상의 집과 백성에게 소식을 전하게 했다.
ko.B: 그들은 사울의 머리를 베고 갑옷을 벗겼다. 그리고 블레셋 땅 곳곳에 사람들을 보내어, 그들의 우상 신전과 백성에게 이 기쁜 소식을 전하게 했다.
ko.R: 그들은 사울의 머리를 베고 갑옷을 벗겨 갔다. 그리고 블레셋 땅 곳곳에 사람들을 보내어, 그들의 우상을 모신 신전과 모든 백성에게 이 기쁜 소식을 전하게 했다.

decisions.choice: sent: sent messengers around the land with the news
alternatives: sent his head and armor around the land
decisions.reason: The verb has no object. It may mean that they sent word by messengers, or that they sent Saul's head and armor around the Philistine towns to be shown. 1 Chronicles 10:9 has the same words. Verse 10 says where the armor ended up.

decisions.choice: to bring the news: to announce a victory as good news
decisions.reason: The verb is used for bringing news, usually good news, and especially news of victory (2 Samuel 18:19-20; Isaiah 52:7). For the Philistines, Saul's death was a triumph to be announced to their gods as well as to their people.

decisions.choice: they cut off his head: what David did to the Philistine champion
decisions.reason: David had cut off Goliath's head and stripped him of his weapons (17:51, 54). Now the Philistines do the same to Israel's king.

decisions.choice: the house of their idols: their temples
decisions.reason: "House" is the usual word for a temple, and "house" here stands for the temples in each town. The word for idols comes from a root linked with shaping and with grief; it is a scornful name for the images of other gods (Hosea 4:17).

decisions.choice: sent messengers
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable supply who was sent; the meaning decision gives the other possibility.

source.text: וַיָּשִׂ֨מוּ֙ אֶת־כֵּלָ֔יו בֵּ֖ית עַשְׁתָּר֑וֹת וְאֶת־גְּוִיָּתוֹ֙ תָּקְע֔וּ בְּחוֹמַ֖ת בֵּ֥ית שָֽׁן׃

records.literal_gloss: And they put his armor [in the] house of Ashtaroth, and his corpse they fastened on [the] wall of Beth-shan.

en.L: And they put his armor in the house of the Ashtaroth, and they fastened his body to the wall of Beth-shan.
en.B: They placed his armor in the temple of the Ashtaroth and fastened his body on the wall of Beth-shan.
en.R: They put his armor in the temple of the goddesses called the Ashtaroth, and they hung his body on the city wall of Beth-shan.

es.L: Y pusieron su armadura en la casa de las Astarot, y clavaron su cadáver en el muro de Bet-sán.
es.B: Pusieron su armadura en el templo de las Astarot y clavaron su cuerpo en el muro de Bet-sán.
es.R: Pusieron su armadura en el templo de las diosas llamadas Astarot, y colgaron su cuerpo en el muro de la ciudad de Bet-sán.

fr.L: Et ils mirent ses armes dans la maison des Ashtaroth, et ils fixèrent son cadavre sur le mur de Beth-Shân.
fr.B: Ils déposèrent ses armes dans le temple des Ashtaroth et fixèrent son corps sur la muraille de Beth-Shân.
fr.R: Ils ont mis ses armes dans le temple des déesses appelées Ashtaroth, et ils ont accroché son corps sur la muraille de la ville de Beth-Shân.

sw.L: Wakaziweka silaha zake katika nyumba ya Ashtarothi, nao wakaufunga mwili wake ukutani mwa Beth-shani.
sw.B: Wakaziweka silaha zake katika hekalu la Ashtarothi, wakaufungia mwili wake katika ukuta wa Beth-shani.
sw.R: Wakaziweka silaha zake katika hekalu la miungu ya kike iitwayo Ashtarothi, wakautundika mwili wake katika ukuta wa mji wa Beth-shani.

vi.L: Họ để áo giáp ông trong đền miếu của các nữ thần Át-tạt-tê, và đóng xác ông vào tường thành Bết-san.
vi.B: Họ đặt áo giáp của ông trong đền miếu các nữ thần Át-tạt-tê, và treo xác ông trên tường thành Bết-san.
vi.R: Họ đặt áo giáp của ông trong đền thờ các nữ thần tên là Át-tạt-tê, và treo xác ông trên tường thành Bết-san.

ko.L: 그리고 그들이 그의 갑옷을 아스다롯의 집에 두고, 그의 시체는 벧산 성벽에 못 박아 걸었다.
ko.B: 그들은 사울의 갑옷을 아스다롯 신전에 두고, 그의 시체는 벧산 성벽에 못 박아 매달았다.
ko.R: 그들은 사울의 갑옷을 아스다롯이라는 여신들의 신전에 두었다. 그리고 그의 시체는 벧산 성의 성벽에 매달았다.

decisions.choice: the house of the Ashtaroth: a temple of the goddess Ashtoreth
decisions.reason: Ashtaroth is the plural of Ashtoreth, a Canaanite goddess of fertility and war, as at 7:3. The armor of the defeated king was placed there as a trophy, just as Goliath's sword had been kept at the sanctuary at Nob (21:10).

decisions.choice: Beth-shan: a walled city at the eastern end of the Jezreel valley, near the Jordan
decisions.reason: This is a shorter spelling of Beth-shean, a town Israel had never taken from the Canaanites (Joshua 17:11-12; Judges 1:27). Hanging the bodies on its wall, where travelers on the main road through the valley would see them, was a public display of shame.

decisions.choice: 1 Chronicles 10:10 tells this differently
decisions.reason: The Chronicler says they put his armor "in the house of their gods" and fastened his head in the house of Dagon. The two accounts complement each other: the head went to Dagon's temple, the body to the wall of Beth-shan. Dagon was the Philistine god whose image had fallen before the ark (5:1-5).

decisions.choice: fastened: fixed firmly, as with a peg or nail
decisions.reason: The verb is used for driving in a tent peg (Judges 4:21) and for fixing something firmly in place (Isaiah 22:23). The body was fixed to the wall so that it could be seen.

decisions.choice: the goddesses called the Ashtaroth
decisions.reason: Readable explains the name as at 7:3.

decisions.choice: his body
decisions.reason: The word means a body, usually a dead one; "body" is the natural word in this context and is used again in verse 12.

decisions.choice: les Ashtaroth; Beth-Shân
decisions.reason: "Ashtaroth" as the French of 1 Samuel 7:3-4 and 12:10 has it, the plural of the goddess's name (m1); Beth-Shân, not in the terms table, in the usual French transcription.

decisions.choice: las Astarot; Bet-sán
decisions.reason: The Hebrew plural names the goddess Ashtoreth in her many images (m1), kept as a plural name with the article, as the English keeps “the Ashtaroth”; Beth-shan (m2) in its usual Spanish form.

decisions.choice: "Ashtarothi"; "Beth-shani"
decisions.reason: Names not in the terms note take a Swahili spelling with a final vowel; Readable explains the Ashtaroth as the English does.

decisions.choice: "các nữ thần Át-tạt-tê"; "Bết-san"
decisions.reason: A temple of the goddess Ashtoreth (m1); the plural is given as "the goddesses" with the name in its usual Protestant form.

decisions.choice: "아스다롯", "벧산"
decisions.reason: The usual Protestant Korean forms; Readable says the Ashtaroth are goddesses, as the English Readable does.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁמְע֣וּ אֵלָ֔יו יֹשְׁבֵ֖י יָבֵ֣ישׁ גִּלְעָ֑ד אֵ֛ת אֲשֶׁר־עָשׂ֥וּ פְלִשְׁתִּ֖ים לְשָׁאֽוּל׃

records.literal_gloss: And heard concerning him [the] inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead what had done Philistines to Saul.

en.L: And the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead heard concerning him what the Philistines had done to Saul.
en.B: The people living in Jabesh-gilead heard what the Philistines had done to Saul.
en.R: The people of the town of Jabesh-gilead heard what the Philistines had done to Saul's body.

es.L: Y oyeron acerca de él los habitantes de Jabes de Galaad lo que los filisteos habían hecho a Saúl.
es.B: Los habitantes de Jabes de Galaad se enteraron de lo que los filisteos le habían hecho a Saúl.
es.R: La gente del pueblo de Jabes de Galaad oyó lo que los filisteos le habían hecho al cuerpo de Saúl.

fr.L: Et les habitants de Yabesh de Galaad apprirent à son sujet ce que les Philistins avaient fait à Saül.
fr.B: Les habitants de Yabesh de Galaad apprirent ce que les Philistins avaient fait à Saül.
fr.R: Les habitants de la ville de Yabesh de Galaad ont appris ce que les Philistins avaient fait au corps de Saül.

sw.L: Wakaaji wa Yabeshi ya Gileadi wakasikia habari zake, yale Wafilisti waliyomtendea Sauli.
sw.B: Watu walioishi Yabeshi ya Gileadi wakasikia yale ambayo Wafilisti walimtendea Sauli.
sw.R: Watu wa mji wa Yabeshi ya Gileadi wakasikia yale ambayo Wafilisti waliutendea mwili wa Sauli.

vi.L: Dân cư Gia-be ở Ga-la-át nghe về ông, về điều người Phi-li-tin đã làm cho Sau-lơ.
vi.B: Dân cư Gia-be ở Ga-la-át nghe tin người Phi-li-tin đã làm gì cho Sau-lơ.
vi.R: Dân thành Gia-be ở Ga-la-át nghe biết người Phi-li-tin đã làm gì với xác Sau-lơ.

ko.L: 그리고 길르앗 야베스 주민들이 블레셋 사람들이 사울에게 한 일에 대하여 들었다.
ko.B: 길르앗 야베스에 사는 사람들은 블레셋 사람들이 사울에게 한 일을 들었다.
ko.R: 길르앗 야베스 마을 사람들은 블레셋 사람들이 사울의 시체에 한 일을 들었다.

decisions.choice: Jabesh-gilead: the town Saul had rescued at the start of his reign
decisions.reason: When Nahash the Ammonite threatened to gouge out the right eye of every man of Jabesh, Saul gathered Israel, marched through the night and saved the town (11:1-11). That rescue first showed Saul to be Israel's king. The town now repays him. The bond between Jabesh and Benjamin, Saul's tribe, went back to Judges 21:8-14.

decisions.choice: concerning him: about Saul
decisions.reason: The pronoun points ahead to Saul, named at the end of the verse. The repetition puts weight on him: what had been done to Saul himself.

decisions.choice: to Saul's body
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that what they heard about was what had been done to the dead king's body (verses 9-10).

decisions.choice: "길르앗 야베스"
decisions.reason: The form the terms of this translation set; the town Saul had rescued at the start of his reign (meaning decision m1).

source.text: וַיָּק֜וּמוּ כָּל־אִ֣ישׁ חַיִל֮ וַיֵּלְכ֣וּ כָל־הַלַּיְלָה֒ וַיִּקְח֞וּ אֶת־גְּוִיַּ֣ת שָׁא֗וּל וְאֵת֙ גְּוִיֹּ֣ת בָּנָ֔יו מֵחוֹמַ֖ת בֵּ֣ית שָׁ֑ן וַיָּבֹ֣אוּ יָבֵ֔שָׁה וַיִּשְׂרְפ֥וּ אֹתָ֖ם שָֽׁם׃

records.literal_gloss: And arose every man of valor and went all the night, and took [the] corpse of Saul and [the] corpses of his sons from [the] wall of Beth-shan, and came to Jabesh and burned them there.

en.L: And every man of valor arose and went all the night, and took the body of Saul and the bodies of his sons from the wall of Beth-shan, and came to Jabesh and burned them there.
en.B: All their brave men set out and traveled all night. They took the body of Saul and the bodies of his sons down from the wall of Beth-shan, brought them to Jabesh, and burned them there.
en.R: All the bravest men of the town set out and walked all night. They took Saul's body and his sons' bodies down from the city wall of Beth-shan. Then they went back to Jabesh and burned the bodies there.

es.L: Y se levantaron todos los hombres valientes, y anduvieron toda la noche, y tomaron el cadáver de Saúl y los cadáveres de sus hijos del muro de Bet-sán, y vinieron a Jabes y los quemaron allí.
es.B: Todos sus hombres valientes se pusieron en marcha y caminaron toda la noche. Bajaron del muro de Bet-sán el cuerpo de Saúl y los cuerpos de sus hijos, los llevaron a Jabes y allí los quemaron.
es.R: Todos los hombres más valientes del pueblo salieron y caminaron toda la noche. Bajaron del muro de la ciudad de Bet-sán el cuerpo de Saúl y los cuerpos de sus hijos. Luego volvieron a Jabes y quemaron allí los cuerpos.

fr.L: Et tous les hommes vaillants se levèrent et marchèrent toute la nuit, et ils prirent le cadavre de Saül et les cadavres de ses fils sur le mur de Beth-Shân, et ils revinrent à Yabesh et les y brûlèrent.
fr.B: Tous leurs hommes vaillants se mirent en route et marchèrent toute la nuit. Ils détachèrent de la muraille de Beth-Shân le corps de Saül et ceux de ses fils, les rapportèrent à Yabesh et les y brûlèrent.
fr.R: Tous les hommes les plus courageux de la ville sont partis et ils ont marché toute la nuit. Ils ont détaché de la muraille de Beth-Shân le corps de Saül et ceux de ses fils. Ensuite, ils sont retournés à Yabesh et ils ont brûlé les corps là-bas.

sw.L: Mashujaa wote wakainuka, wakaenda usiku kucha, wakauchukua mwili wa Sauli na miili ya wanawe kutoka ukutani mwa Beth-shani, wakaja Yabeshi, wakaiteketeza huko.
sw.B: Mashujaa wao wote wakaondoka, wakasafiri usiku kucha. Wakaushusha mwili wa Sauli na miili ya wanawe kutoka ukutani mwa Beth-shani, wakaileta Yabeshi, wakaiteketeza huko.
sw.R: Wanaume wote mashujaa zaidi wa mji ule wakaondoka, wakatembea usiku kucha. Wakaushusha mwili wa Sauli na miili ya wanawe kutoka ukutani mwa mji wa Beth-shani. Kisha wakarudi Yabeshi, wakaichoma miili hiyo huko.

vi.L: Mọi dũng sĩ đứng dậy đi suốt đêm, lấy xác Sau-lơ và xác các con trai ông khỏi tường thành Bết-san, rồi đến Gia-be và thiêu họ ở đó.
vi.B: Tất cả những dũng sĩ của họ lên đường, đi suốt đêm. Họ gỡ xác Sau-lơ và xác các con trai ông khỏi tường thành Bết-san, đem về Gia-be và thiêu ở đó.
vi.R: Tất cả những người dũng cảm nhất trong thành lên đường và đi suốt đêm. Họ gỡ xác Sau-lơ và xác các con trai ông xuống khỏi tường thành Bết-san. Rồi họ trở về Gia-be và thiêu các xác ấy ở đó.

ko.L: 그러자 용사들이 모두 일어나 밤새도록 가서, 사울의 시체와 그의 아들들의 시체를 벧산 성벽에서 거두어 야베스로 와서, 그곳에서 그것들을 불살랐다.
ko.B: 그곳의 용사들이 모두 일어나 밤새도록 걸어가서, 사울의 시체와 그의 아들들의 시체를 벧산 성벽에서 내려 야베스로 가져왔다. 그리고 그곳에서 시체를 불살랐다.
ko.R: 그 마을의 가장 용감한 사람들이 모두 길을 떠나 밤새도록 걸어갔다. 그들은 벧산 성벽에서 사울의 시체와 그의 아들들의 시체를 내렸다. 그리고 야베스로 돌아와서 그곳에서 시체를 불태웠다.

decisions.choice: every man of valor: all the town's fighting men, men of courage and strength
decisions.reason: The phrase describes men able and brave enough for a dangerous task. They had to go into territory now held by the Philistines and take the bodies from a guarded city wall.

decisions.choice: they went all night, as Saul had once come by night to save them
decisions.reason: Saul had marched his army through the night and attacked the Ammonites in the morning watch to save Jabesh (11:9-11). Now its men travel by night to rescue his body. The journey from Jabesh to Beth-shan, across the Jordan, was long enough to take the whole night.

decisions.choice: burned them there: an unusual act, probably because of the state of the bodies
alternatives: they burned spices for them, as at a king's funeral (2 Chronicles 16:14)
decisions.reason: Israelites normally buried their dead, and burning a body was usually a punishment (Leviticus 20:14; Joshua 7:25; Amos 2:1). The bodies had been mutilated and left exposed, and burning may have been done to clean them of the disgrace or because they had begun to decay. The bones were kept and buried (verse 13). 1 Chronicles 10:12 does not mention the burning.

decisions.choice: their brave men; the bravest men of the town; took ... down from
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear that these are the men of Jabesh, and say "down from" since the bodies were hanging on the wall.

ko.B: 그들은 그 뼈를 거두어 야베스에 있는 에셀 나무 아래에 묻고, 칠 일 동안 금식했다.
ko.R: 그러고 나서 그들은 뼈를 거두어 야베스의 에셀 나무 아래에 묻었다. 그리고 슬퍼하는 마음으로 칠 일 동안 아무것도 먹지 않았다.

decisions.choice: the tamarisk: a known tree in Jabesh, a place of honor
decisions.reason: The tamarisk was a desert tree with feathery leaves. The article points to a particular tree that the people of the town knew. Great trees marked places of honor and burial (Genesis 35:8), and Saul himself had held court under a tamarisk at Gibeah (22:6). 1 Chronicles 10:12 names the tree with a word for a large tree, often rendered "oak".

decisions.choice: they fasted seven days: they mourned as for a great man
decisions.reason: Seven days was a full time of mourning (Genesis 50:10). Fasting showed grief and honor for the dead (2 Samuel 1:12; 3:35).

decisions.choice: the bones of Saul and his sons were later moved
decisions.reason: David thanked the men of Jabesh for their loyalty in burying Saul (2 Samuel 2:4-7). Later he took the bones of Saul and Jonathan from Jabesh and buried them in the tomb of Saul's father Kish in Benjamin (2 Samuel 21:12-14). With this verse the book of 1 Samuel ends; the story goes straight on in 2 Samuel 1:1, where David, back at Ziklag, hears the news.

decisions.choice: did not eat ... to show their sorrow
decisions.reason: Readable explains what fasting meant here.
